meaning: honest, down-to-earth (people); solid, good value (food, goods)

senses.en: honest, genuine, down-to-earth (a person, or the way they talk)
solid, no-frills, good value (food, goods, a deal)

examples.zh: 小王这个人很实在。
examples.en: Xiao Wang is a very genuine, down-to-earth person.
examples.analysis: 实在 (shízai, light second syllable) is an adjective after 很 describing character: honest, no pretence, means what he says. 小王这个人 'Xiao Wang, this person' is a common way to open a comment on someone's character.

examples.zh: 这家店的菜很实在，也不贵。
examples.en: The food at this place is hearty and generous, and it isn't expensive either.
examples.analysis: Said of food or goods, 实在 means solid and honest: decent portions, real ingredients, nothing just for show. 家 is the measure word for shops and restaurants (这家店 'this place'). 也不贵 adds a second point: 'and it isn't expensive either'.

examples.zh: 他说话不太实在，你别全信。
examples.en: He doesn't always tell it straight, so don't believe everything he says.
examples.analysis: 说话实在 means talking plainly and honestly, without exaggeration or empty promises; 不太实在 softens the criticism to 'not very'. 别全信 'don't believe it all': 全 'entirely' goes before the verb 信 'believe'.

collocations.en: the food is hearty and generous

related.en: adverb: really, truly (实在太累了 'I'm really too tired'); full fourth tone on 在
honest, well-behaved; can also suggest naive
serious, conscientious about doing things properly

meaning: full; filled up, with no room left

senses.en: full (a cup, a bus, a hotel, a class)
after a verb: filled to the top (倒满 'pour full', 坐满 'every seat taken')

examples.zh: 公交车已经满了，等下一辆吧。
examples.en: The bus is already full. Let's wait for the next one.
examples.analysis: 满了 'has become full': 了 marks the change, so no 很 is needed. 已经 'already' goes before it. 下一辆 'the next one' uses 辆, the measure word for vehicles, and leaves out the noun because both sides know it is a bus.

examples.zh: 酒店房间都满了吗？
examples.en: Are all the rooms at the hotel full?
examples.analysis: For hotels, restaurants and classes, 满了 means 'fully booked; no space left'. 都 'all' sums up the plural subject 房间 'rooms' and goes before the predicate. 吗 turns the whole statement into a yes-no question.

examples.zh: 别倒那么满，我喝不完。
examples.en: Don't pour it so full. I can't finish it all.
examples.analysis: 倒满 'pour until full' is verb + result. With 那么 'so' in front of 满, 别倒那么满 means 'don't pour it that full'; 别 makes it a request. 喝不完 'can't finish drinking it' gives the reason: verb + 不 + 完.

collocations.en: to fill (a glass) to the top

meaning: fake, false; not real or not true

senses.en: fake, imitation (goods, flowers, money)
false, untrue (what someone says)

examples.zh: 这个包是假的吧？
examples.en: This bag is a fake, isn't it?
examples.analysis: 是假的 'is fake' is the usual way to say something isn't genuine: 是 + adjective + 的 'a fake one'. 吧 at the end asks for confirmation of something you already suspect, unlike a neutral 吗 question.

examples.zh: 他说的都是假的。
examples.en: None of what he said was true.
examples.analysis: 他说的 'what he said' is a 的 phrase used as the subject. 都 'all' covers everything in it, and 是假的 says it is untrue. Of statements, 假 means 'false'; of objects, it means 'fake'.

examples.zh: 这些花是假的？看着像真的！
examples.en: These flowers are fake? They look real!
examples.analysis: A statement with a question mark shows surprise: 'these are fake?'. 假 and 真 are a pair: 假的 'a fake one', 真的 'a real one'. 看着像… 'looks like…' adds 着 to 看 to mean 'judging by looks'.

collocations.en: real or fake; true or false

related.en: holiday; vacation: here 假 is read jià
to have a holiday or a day off (also jià)

meaning: in front of (someone); in someone's presence

senses.en: the space right in front of a person (在我面前 'in front of me')
in the presence of others (在大家面前 'in front of everyone')

examples.zh: 别在孩子面前说这些。
examples.en: Don't talk about this in front of the kids.
examples.analysis: 在 + person + 面前 'in front of someone' says where the action happens and comes before the verb 说. Here it means 'in their presence, where they can hear'. 别 at the start makes it a request: 'don't'.

examples.zh: 他就在你面前，你没看见吗？
examples.en: He's right in front of you. Didn't you see him?
examples.analysis: Here 在 is the main verb 'to be at': 他在你面前 'he is in front of you', and 就 adds 'right'. 面前 mostly goes with people, or with things set right before someone (摆在面前); to say where a building or place is, use 前边 (银行前边 'in front of the bank').

examples.zh: 在大家面前唱歌，我有点儿怕。
examples.en: I'm a bit scared of singing in front of everyone.
examples.analysis: 在大家面前唱歌 'singing in front of everyone' is the topic, put first; 我有点儿怕 'I'm a little scared' comments on it. 有点儿 + adjective or feeling means 'a bit', and it usually goes with unwelcome feelings.

related.en: in front (of a place or thing): 银行前边

meaning: correct; right (an answer, a method, a choice)

senses.en: correct, without mistakes (an answer, pronunciation, a sentence)
right, sound (a choice or a way of doing things)

examples.zh: 你这么做是正确的。
examples.en: You were right to do it this way.
examples.analysis: 你这么做 'you doing it this way' is the subject, and 是正确的 gives the verdict: 'was right'. 是…的 makes the judgment sound firm and settled. In casual chat 对 is more common (你这么做是对的); 正确 sounds more considered.

examples.zh: 这个读音不正确，再说一遍。
examples.en: That pronunciation isn't correct. Say it again.
examples.analysis: 不正确 'not correct' is the plain negative: 不 goes straight before the adjective. 正确 suits things checked against a standard, like answers and pronunciation. 再说一遍 'say it once more': 遍 counts one full time through.

examples.zh: 老师，这个句子正确吗？
examples.en: Teacher, is this sentence correct?
examples.analysis: 正确 is the predicate, and 吗 makes it a yes-no question. A student could also ask 对吗; 正确吗 sounds a little more careful, which fits checking written work. 老师 at the start addresses the teacher directly.

collocations.en: the right way to do it

meaning: to agree to, say yes to; to promise; to answer when called

senses.en: to agree to, say yes to (a request)
to promise (答应 + someone, or + an action)
to answer when someone calls your name

examples.zh: 他答应明天来帮忙。
examples.en: He promised to come and help tomorrow.
examples.analysis: 答应 takes a whole action as its object: 答应 + 明天来帮忙 'to come and help tomorrow'. It usually implies someone asked and he said yes, which makes it a promise rather than just a plan.

examples.zh: 你答应我的事，别忘了！
examples.en: Don't forget what you promised me!
examples.analysis: 你答应我的事 'the thing you promised me' is a 的 phrase: the clause 你答应我 describes 事. It comes first as the topic, and 别忘了 'don't forget' comments on it. 答应 + person means 'promise someone'.

examples.zh: 我叫了他两次，他都没答应。
examples.en: I called out to him twice, and he didn't answer either time.
examples.analysis: Here 答应 means to answer when someone calls your name, as in replying 'Yes?'. 没答应 'didn't answer' uses 没 for something that did not happen. 都 points back to 两次: 'neither time'.

collocations.en: to say yes to it (and commit)

related.en: to answer a question; 答应 answers a call or a request
to agree (with an idea or a plan)
to accept (an invitation, a gift, advice)

meaning: to accept, take (payment, gifts); to bring in, put away

senses.en: to accept, take (payment, a gift, credit cards)
to bring in, collect, put away (laundry, things)

examples.zh: 你们收信用卡吗？
examples.en: Do you take credit cards?
examples.analysis: 收 here means a shop 'takes, accepts' a form of payment, as in 收钱 'take payment'. 你们 'you (plural)' addresses the shop as a business, not only the cashier. 吗 makes it a yes-no question.

examples.zh: 要下雨了，快去收衣服！
examples.en: It's about to rain. Go and bring the laundry in, quick!
examples.analysis: 收衣服 means to take in clothes, usually laundry hanging out to dry; 收 is 'gather in, put away'. 要…了 'about to' gives the reason, and 快去 + verb 'hurry and go do' makes it an urgent request.

examples.zh: 这个礼物太贵了，我不能收。
examples.en: This gift is too expensive. I can't accept it.
examples.analysis: 收 means 'accept' something offered. 不能收 'can't accept' is the usual polite refusal of a gift or money: 能 says it would not be right, not that it is impossible. 这个礼物太贵了 'this gift is too expensive' gives the reason first.

related.en: to receive (a message, a parcel): 收 + result 到

meaning: street

senses.en: street (a road lined with shops and houses)

examples.zh: 这条街晚上人很多。
examples.en: There are lots of people on this street in the evening.
examples.analysis: 条 is the measure word for long, narrow things, so 这条街 'this street'. The sentence is topic + comment: 这条街 is the topic, 晚上 adds the time, and 人很多 'there are a lot of people' is the comment.

examples.zh: 银行在哪条街？
examples.en: Which street is the bank on?
examples.analysis: 哪 + measure word + noun asks 'which one': 哪条街 'which street'. 在 is the main verb, 'to be located at'. Chinese uses 在 where English says 'on' a street: 在这条街 'on this street'.

examples.zh: 我家那条街没有超市。
examples.en: There's no supermarket on the street where I live.
examples.analysis: 我家那条街, literally 'my home, that street', means 'the street I live on': 那 + 条 points to a street both people can picture. 没有 'there isn't' is the negative of 有 'there is'.

collocations.en: on the street; out in town
to go shopping; to stroll around the shops

meaning: to borrow; to lend (借给)

senses.en: to borrow (跟 someone 借 something)
to lend (借给 + person)

examples.zh: 你的笔能借我用用吗？
examples.en: Could I borrow your pen for a moment?
examples.analysis: 借我用用 'lend it to me to use a bit': 借 + person + 用用. The doubled verb 用用 makes the request small and casual. 你的笔 comes first as the topic: 'your pen, can you lend it to me?'

examples.zh: 我跟他借了两百块钱，明天还他。
examples.en: I borrowed two hundred yuan from him. I'll pay him back tomorrow.
examples.analysis: 跟他借 'borrow from him': 跟 + person marks the lender, so the direction is clear. Without 跟, 借他两百块 can mean 'borrow from him' or 'lend him', so use 跟…借 to borrow and 借给 to lend. 还他 'pay him back'. 块 is the spoken word for yuan.

examples.zh: 图书馆的书可以借多久？
examples.en: How long can you borrow library books for?
examples.analysis: 借 + 多久 'borrow for how long': the length of time comes right after the verb. 图书馆的书 'the library's books' is the topic, so no 'you' is needed: 'library books, can be borrowed for how long?'

related.en: to give back; to return (还书, 还钱)
to rent: you pay to use it
to give as a gift: nothing comes back

meaning: to put down; to let go of (a worry, an idea)

senses.en: to put down, set down (something in your hand)
to let go of, stop dwelling on (a worry, a grudge)

examples.zh: 先放下手机，吃饭了！
examples.en: Put your phone down first. It's time to eat!
examples.analysis: 放下 + object: 放 'put' + 下 'down' as the result, so the thing leaves your hands. 先 'first' says do this before anything else. 吃饭了 is the usual call to the table: 'time to eat!'

examples.zh: 他放下电话就走了。
examples.en: He put down the phone and left right away.
examples.analysis: 放下电话 'put the phone down' can mean hanging up (挂电话 is the usual phrase for that). First action + 就 + second action says the second came straight after: 'as soon as he put the phone down, he left'. 了 marks the leaving as done.

examples.zh: 放下吧，别想那么多了。
examples.en: Let it go. Stop thinking about it so much.
examples.analysis: With no object, 放下 here means 'let it go': put down a worry, not a thing. 吧 makes it gentle advice. 别…了 'stop doing…' asks someone to stop what they are already doing: 别想那么多了 'stop overthinking'.

collocations.en: to put the phone down; to hang up

related.en: to stop worrying; to feel at ease

meaning: at the same time; (linking clauses) at the same time, also

senses.en: the same moment: 同时 + verb 'at the same time'
at the same time; also (adds a second fact)

examples.zh: 我们是同时到的。
examples.en: We arrived at the same time.
examples.analysis: 同时 'at the same time' comes before the verb 到 'arrive'. 是…的 frames a past event and puts the focus on one detail inside it, here the timing: it was at the same time that we arrived.

examples.zh: 别同时做两件事。
examples.en: Don't do two things at once.
examples.analysis: 同时 sits between 别 and the verb, like an adverb: 'don't at-the-same-time do'. 两件事 'two things' uses 两, not 二, before a measure word, and 件 is the measure word for matters and tasks.

examples.zh: 这个工作很累，同时也很有意思。
examples.en: This job is tiring, but at the same time it's really interesting.
examples.analysis: At the start of a clause, 同时 links two facts that are both true: 'at the same time'. It often pairs with 也 'also'. Here the two facts pull in different directions, so English adds 'but'.

collocations.en: and at the same time also
while …; at the same time as …
to happen at the same time

related.en: doing two things at once (一边吃一边看)

meaning: a day, a date; (one's) days, life

senses.en: a particular day or date (a special day, a day to agree on)
life; the days one lives through (现在的日子 'life now')

examples.zh: 今天是什么日子？这么多人！
examples.en: What's the occasion today? There are so many people!
examples.analysis: 什么日子 'what day' asks whether today is a special day, such as a holiday or festival, not the calendar date (for that, ask 几号). 这么多人 'so many people' is the reason for asking.

examples.zh: 我们找个日子一起吃饭吧。
examples.en: Let's find a day to have a meal together.
examples.analysis: 找个日子 'find a day': 个 stands for 一个, and the 一 is often dropped in speech. 日子 here is a day still to be agreed on. 吧 makes the whole thing a friendly suggestion: 'let's…'.

examples.zh: 现在的日子比以前好多了。
examples.en: Life now is much better than it used to be.
examples.analysis: 日子 here means daily life, how people live. 现在的日子 'life now' is compared with 以前 'before' using A 比 B + adjective. 好多了 'much better': 多了 after an adjective in a comparison means 'much more so'.

collocations.en: to live one's life; to get by

related.en: day as a unit of time (三天 'three days')

meaning: measure word for mountains, buildings, bridges, cities

senses.en: for large things fixed in place: mountains, buildings, bridges, cities

examples.zh: 前边那座楼是医院吗？
examples.en: Is that building up ahead the hospital?
examples.analysis: 座 counts big things fixed in place, like buildings and mountains: 那 + 座 + 楼 'that building'. 那个楼 is also heard in casual speech. 前边 'up ahead' comes first and tells the listener where to look.

examples.zh: 我家后边有一座小山。
examples.en: There's a small hill behind my house.
examples.analysis: 一座小山 'a small hill': number + 座 + noun, with 小 'small' before 山. 有 here means 'there is', and the place 我家后边 'behind my house' comes first, as Chinese puts the location before 有.

examples.zh: 这座楼有二十层。
examples.en: This building has twenty floors.
examples.analysis: 座 counts the building as a whole; 层 counts its floors. 有 here means 'has'. 二十层 'twenty floors' needs no other measure word, because 层 is itself the measure for floors.

meaning: for example; such as, like

senses.en: for example; such as (before one or more examples)
比如什么? 'like what?' (asking for examples)

examples.zh: 多做运动，比如走路、爬山。
examples.en: Get more exercise, such as walking or hiking.
examples.analysis: 比如 brings in examples after a general statement: 运动 'exercise' first, then 比如 + 走路、爬山. The list comma 、 separates items in a list. 多 + verb at the start means 'do more': 多做运动 'exercise more'.

examples.zh: 好多东西都能在网上买，比如衣服和鞋。
examples.en: You can buy lots of things online, like clothes and shoes.
examples.analysis: The examples follow the main clause, introduced by 比如: 'like clothes and shoes'. 和 joins the two nouns. 好多 'lots of' is a casual alternative to 很多, and 都 sums up the many things before the verb.

examples.zh: 你说有好多问题，比如什么？
examples.en: You say there are lots of problems. Like what?
examples.analysis: 比如什么? 'like what?' asks someone to back up a vague claim with examples; it is a natural follow-up in conversation. 你说有… 'you say there are…' repeats their words before asking.

related.en: like, such as (像衣服、鞋这样的东西 'things like clothes and shoes')
for example; more formal, mostly written

meaning: to affect, disturb; influence, effect

senses.en: to affect, have an effect on (often a bad one)
to disturb, bother (other people)
influence, effect (对…影响很大 'a big effect on…')

examples.zh: 晚上喝茶会影响睡觉。
examples.en: Drinking tea in the evening can affect your sleep.
examples.analysis: The subject is a whole action, 晚上喝茶 'drinking tea in the evening', with no extra word needed. 会 'is likely to' + 影响 + 睡觉 'affect sleep'. Used as a verb like this, 影响 usually means a bad effect.

examples.zh: 小声一点儿，别影响别人。
examples.en: Keep it down a bit. Don't disturb other people.
examples.analysis: 影响 + person means 'to disturb, bother' someone; 别影响别人 is a common, friendly reminder in shared spaces (signs use the more polite 请不要影响别人). 小声一点儿 'a bit quieter': an adjective + 一点儿 asks for a little more of that quality.

examples.zh: 下雨对你们影响大吗？
examples.en: Does the rain affect you much?
examples.analysis: Here 影响 is a noun, 'effect': 对你们影响大吗? 'is the effect on you big?'. 对 + person marks who is affected, 大 'big' gives the size of the effect, and 吗 makes it a yes-no question.

meaning: meter (unit of length or height)

senses.en: meter: for length, distance and height (三百米, 一米八)

examples.zh: 他一米八，很高。
examples.en: He's 1.8 meters tall, really tall.
examples.analysis: Height in speech: 一米八 = 1.80 m. The number after 米 gives the decimal part, so 一米七五 is 1.75 m. No verb is needed: 他一米八 'he is 1.8 m'. 很高 'very tall' comments on it.

examples.zh: 地铁站离这儿就三百米，走路去吧。
examples.en: The subway station is only 300 meters from here. Let's walk.
examples.analysis: A 离 B + distance: 地铁站离这儿 + 三百米 'the station is 300 m from here'. 米 follows the number directly, like any measure word. 就 before a number means 'only, just', which is why walking makes sense.

examples.zh: 再走五十米就到了，加油！
examples.en: Just fifty more meters and we're there. Keep going!
examples.analysis: 再 + verb + distance + 就到了 'go another … and you arrive'. 米 follows the number directly, like any measure word. 加油 is the usual cheer to keep someone going.

related.en: cooked rice: here 米 means rice

meaning: interesting; fun, amusing

senses.en: interesting, fun (a film, a class, a job)
amusing, a bit unusual (of a person); can be fond or ironic

examples.zh: 这个电影挺有意思的。
examples.en: This movie's pretty interesting.
examples.analysis: 挺…的 'quite, pretty' wraps around 有意思: 挺有意思的 'pretty interesting', a relaxed, typical spoken compliment. 有意思 works like an adjective, so degree words such as 挺 and 很 go before it.

examples.zh: 你觉得他的课有意思吗？
examples.en: Do you find his classes interesting?
examples.analysis: 你觉得…吗? 'do you think…?' asks for an opinion. 有意思 is the predicate of 他的课 'his classes'. The opposite answer is 没意思 'boring', where 没 replaces 有.

examples.zh: 你这个人真有意思！
examples.en: You're a funny one!
examples.analysis: Said of a person, 有意思 means amusing or a bit unusual. 你这个人 'you, as a person' puts the focus on character. Depending on tone, it can be fond or mildly sarcastic, much like English 'you're a funny one'.

related.en: meaning (什么意思? 'what does it mean?')

meaning: to use (more formal than 用)

senses.en: to use, operate (phones, cards, machines, tools); formal or written in tone

examples.zh: 上课的时候请不要使用手机。
examples.en: Please don't use your phone during class.
examples.analysis: 请不要 + verb 'please do not' is the polite form of a rule, used on signs, in announcements and by teachers. 使用 fits that formal tone; between friends you would say 别用手机. 上课的时候 'during class' comes first and sets the time.

examples.zh: 请问，信用卡在国外能使用吗？
examples.en: Excuse me, can credit cards be used abroad?
examples.analysis: 请问 'excuse me, may I ask' makes this a polite question to staff, for example at a bank, where the more formal 使用 fits; with a friend you would just say 能用吗. 信用卡 is the topic: 'credit cards, can they be used abroad?'. 能 'can' + 使用 asks whether they work there.

examples.zh: 这个洗衣机怎么使用？你能教我吗？
examples.en: How do I use this washing machine? Can you show me?
examples.analysis: 怎么使用 'how to use' asks for the method. 使用 is a little formal here, as in a polite question to a host; between friends 怎么用 is more usual. 能…吗 'can you…?' politely asks for help, and 教 means 'teach, show'.

meaning: aspect, respect, side (of a matter); area, field

senses.en: aspect, respect (别的方面 'in other respects')
area, field (of knowledge or work: 这方面 'this area')

examples.zh: 这个工作别的方面都好，但是钱少。
examples.en: This job is fine in every other way, but the pay is low.
examples.analysis: 别的方面 'other aspects' covers everything except one point, and 都好 says they are all good. 但是 then brings in the exception: 钱少 'the money is little'. 这个工作 is the topic the whole sentence comments on.

examples.zh: 学汉语，你觉得哪方面最难？
examples.en: When it comes to learning Chinese, which part do you find hardest?
examples.analysis: 哪方面 'which aspect' asks someone to pick one part of a bigger topic. 学汉语 at the start is the topic: 'as for learning Chinese'. 最难 'the hardest' is the superlative: 最 + adjective.

examples.zh: 这方面的事你问他吧，他比我懂。
examples.en: For this kind of thing, ask him. He knows more about it than I do.
examples.analysis: 这方面的事 'matters in this area' uses 方面 for a field of knowledge. It is the topic, placed first, and 你问他吧 'ask him' is a suggestion. 他比我懂 'he understands it better than I do' uses A 比 B + verb.

collocations.en: in this respect; in this area
on the one hand … on the other

meaning: bank

senses.en: bank (the company or a branch)

measure.note: 一家银行 'a bank'; 个 is also used

examples.zh: 这儿离银行远吗？
examples.en: Is the bank far from here?
examples.analysis: 离 'from' links two places: 这儿离银行 'here from the bank' + 远吗 'far?'. Either place can come first; 银行离这儿远吗 means the same. 吗 turns it into a yes-no question.

examples.zh: 我下午去银行，你要一起去吗？
examples.en: I'm going to the bank this afternoon. Want to come along?
examples.analysis: 去 + place 'go to the bank' needs no word for 'to'. 下午 'this afternoon' comes before the verb, as time words do. 你要一起去吗? 'do you want to go together?' is a casual invitation.

examples.zh: 这家银行人太多了，我们明天再来吧。
examples.en: This bank is way too crowded. Let's come back tomorrow.
examples.analysis: 家 is the measure word for businesses: 这家银行 'this bank (branch)'. 人太多了 'too many people' is the comment on it. 明天再来 'come again tomorrow': 再 marks an action repeated in the future.

related.en: to take out, withdraw (取钱 'withdraw cash')
